summary: General CA variables (RPM / container): `aap_ca_cert_file`/`ca_tls_cert` and `aap_ca_key_file`/`ca_tls_key` make the installer sign every service certificate with your CA; `aap_ca_cert_files_remote`/`ca_tls_remote` (default false) says whether they're on the remote server. RPM-only: `aap_ca_cert_size` and `aap_service_cert_size` (4096), `aap_ca_passphrase_cipher` (aes256), `aap_ca_regenerate` and `aap_service_regen_cert` (false).
questions: What is ca_tls_cert in containerized AAP?
How do I regenerate the AAP internal CA?
How do I regenerate component certificates in AAP?
What key size does the AAP internal CA use?

answer_card.title: CA and certificate variables
answer_card.answer_md:
| RPM | Container | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `aap_ca_cert_file` | `ca_tls_cert` | – |
| `aap_ca_key_file` | `ca_tls_key` | – |
| `aap_ca_cert_files_remote` | `ca_tls_remote` | `false` |
| `aap_ca_cert_size` | – | `4096` |
| `aap_ca_passphrase_cipher` | – | `aes256` |
| `aap_ca_regenerate` | – | `false` |
| `aap_service_cert_size` | – | `4096` |
| `aap_service_regen_cert` | – | `false` |

With a CA cert and key set you don't need per-service `*_tls_cert` variables.
